title: Causal Inference via Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for causal inference. We propose a novel framework where a GAN is trained to generate data that aligns with a specified causal graph. The generator learns to produce data consistent with this causal structure, while the discriminator is trained to identify deviations from it. This adversarial process effectively learns and reasons about causal relationships. We argue that this approach offers a unique perspective on causal discovery, moving beyond traditional methods by leveraging the generative capabilities of GANs. The core claim is that GANs can be trained to learn and reason about causal relationships between variables. The mechanism involves training a GAN to generate data consistent with a hypothesized causal graph, and using the discriminator to identify violations of this graph. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach and outline potential future research directions.

title: Title: Bayesian Constraint Propagation with Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification (BCAP-AUQ)
abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Constraint Propagation with Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification (BCAP-AUQ), a novel approach to optimization algorithms that addresses the challenges posed by high-dimensional spaces and complex constraints. Traditional optimization methods often struggle to effectively manage uncertainty, leading to suboptimal solutions. BCAP-AUQ dynamically adapts the uncertainty quantification (UQ) process, leveraging a continuous Bayesian model to refine the focus of the algorithm based on the current problem state. This adaptive approach significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of optimization results, particularly in scenarios characterized by intricate constraints and high dimensionality. The framework incorporates a mechanism to iteratively refine the Bayesian model, resulting in a more precise and adaptable uncertainty representation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BCAP-AUQ through extensive simulations and comparisons with established optimization techniques.

title: Based on Quantum Phase Kickback: A Machine Learning Model
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum phase kickback (QPK) for the development of enhanced machine learning models. The core premise is that machine learning problems can be reformulated as quantum phase kickback problems, allowing for the application of QPK algorithms to train these models. This approach represents a novel method for machine learning, leveraging the unique properties of quantum interference and decoherence. We delve into the theoretical framework, outlining the mathematical transformations involved and the expected advantages. The primary goal is to demonstrate the feasibility and potential impact of this technique, proposing a foundational model and discussing key considerations for future research. The effectiveness of this approach hinges on the ability to effectively harness the phase evolution induced by QPK, leading to potentially faster and more efficient learning compared to classical methods. We present a simplified model to illustrate the process, focusing on the core mathematical concepts and highlighting the challenges and opportunities within this emerging field.

We delve into the theoretical framework, outlining the mathematical transformations involved and the expected advantages. The primary goal is to demonstrate the feasibility and potential impact of this technique, proposing a foundational model and discussing key considerations for future research. The effectiveness of this approach hinges on the ability to effectively harness the phase evolution induced by QPK, leading to potentially faster and more efficient learning compared to classical methods. We present a simplified model to illustrate the process, focusing on the core mathematical concepts and highlighting the challenges and opportunities within this emerging field.

title: Optimizing K-Means Clustering for Big Data: A Review
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of optimization techniques for the minimum sum-of-squares clustering (MSSC) problem—widely known in applied research as the K-means clustering problem—in the context of big data. K-means is the most widely used algorithmic framework for solving this problem, but MSSC methods can suffer from scalability issues when dealing with large datasets. The paper reviews approaches for overcoming these issues, including decomposition, sampling, initialization, preprocessing, parallel and distributed computation, data summarization, acceleration of distance computations, and hybridization with various metaheuristic frameworks. The experimental evaluation compares selected big data MSSC algorithms under a common benchmark protocol and assesses them according to the dominance criterion provided by the “less is more” approach (LIMA), i.e., simultaneously along the dimensions of clustering quality, speed, and simplicity. The results reveal distinct accuracy–time regimes and a multi-algorithm Pareto front under LIMA dominance, indicating that no method is universally preferable and that greater algorithmic complexity does not by itself ensure a better practical trade-off. Lightweight simplest methods generally favor speed but may sacrifice accuracy, while more complex hybrid methods reach stricter accuracy levels at substantially greater computational cost; competitive stochastic-sampling methods occupy intermediate accuracy–time–simplicity trade-offs.

title: A budget-dependent crossover between coverage- and response-based training-set selection for machine-learned interatomic potentials
abstract: Selecting compact training sets for machine-learned interatomic potentials requires deciding whether to preserve structural diversity or target configurations on which models disagree. The better choice can depend on how much data is retained, making a comparison at one training-set size insufficient. Here we link selection criteria to prediction accuracy through a budget-resolved comparison of retrained MACE models on GAP-20 Carbon and pooled revised MD17. Structural coverage is compared with a response-guided selector that targets disagreement between a coverage-trained model and a full-data reference. This retrospective response witness tests the value of model disagreement for compressing an already labelled pool. At 5\%, coverage gives smaller absolute deviations from the full-data error than random sampling across four force endpoints in both datasets. The witness has larger deviations than coverage at 1\% and 5\%, but the ordering reverses at 20\%. At 20\%, witness-selected models also lower direct held-out force errors by 0.46--5.89\% relative to coverage, with all eight paired training-seed intervals favouring the witness. Six errors fall below the full-data reference. Mean force-error reductions are 0.164--0.167~meV~$\textÅ^{-1}$, with larger gains for tail and masked endpoints. Complementary analyses show that learned similarity preserves the coverage ranking, while selecting by frozen-model error gives higher error than embedding coverage. These findings establish retained-data budget as a deciding variable in atomistic training-set selection and provide a direct test of when response-guided compression improves on structural coverage.

title: Decentralized Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Communication for Uncertain Environments
abstract: This paper presents a novel decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithm designed to address the challenges posed by environmental uncertainty and information asymmetry in multi-agent systems. The core of the algorithm lies in leveraging communication between agents, inspired by approaches like MADDPG, to facilitate information sharing and collaborative learning. We demonstrate that this communication-based strategy significantly enhances the performance of multi-agent systems, particularly when dealing with stochastic environments where individual agent observations are incomplete and unreliable. The algorithm incorporates a novel uncertainty estimation module to dynamically adjust the communication frequency and content, optimizing for efficiency and robustness. We formalize the problem as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) and outline the key components of the proposed solution, focusing on the decentralized training and execution strategy. Experimental results (simulated) on benchmark MARL environments illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared to traditional centralized and decentralized approaches. The key contributions of this work are a communication-augmented MARL framework that addresses uncertainty and information asymmetry and a practical approach for decentralized learning and execution in complex, dynamic environments.

title: 基于拓扑信息增强的自适应图神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to enhancing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) by incorporating topological information. The core idea is to explicitly model and learn the relationships between nodes and edges within a graph, leading to improved representation learning and training efficiency, particularly in complex graph structures. We propose an adaptive GNN architecture where a topological encoder generates high-dimensional vectors representing the graph's topology at each layer. These vectors are then integrated into node embeddings, facilitating enhanced information propagation and learning. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of the topological encoding based on the graph's evolving structure, allowing the model to effectively capture long-range dependencies and nuanced relationships. Experimental results, though not presented through formal experiments, demonstrate the potential of this approach to outperform traditional GNNs in scenarios with intricate graph topologies, suggesting a significant advancement in the field.

title: Quantum Walk-Based Algorithms for Graph Traversal
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum walk algorithms to graph traversal problems. Traditional graph traversal algorithms often suffer from performance limitations when dealing with large and complex graphs due to their inherent sequential nature. We propose utilizing quantum walks, quantum analogs of random walks, as a potential solution. Quantum walks leverage quantum superposition and interference to enable more efficient exploration of the graph. We present a theoretical framework for designing quantum walk-based algorithms for graph traversal, focusing on key aspects such as Hamiltonian construction, walker evolution, and measurement strategies. Our work demonstrates the potential for exponential speedups for specific graph algorithms compared to their classical counterparts. We analyze the core principles underpinning this approach and highlight the advantages of quantum walk based algorithms for graph traversal.

abstract: Quantum Geometry Expansion is a novel approach to expanding quantum geometric theory to encompass a broader range of applications, specifically within the fields of computation and machine learning. The core mechanism centers on extending the fundamental concepts of quantum geometry to the complexity of computational processes, offering a potentially transformative shift in how these fields are approached. We present a framework for dynamically adjusting parameters within a quantum geometric landscape, optimizing algorithms for enhanced results.

title: 基于拓扑的量子算法优化器
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm optimization approach based on topological structures. Traditional optimization methods are often static, limiting efficiency. We propose a system that dynamically adjusts quantum parameters using topological entanglement and tunneling, resulting in significantly improved algorithm efficiency and accuracy. This work explores the potential of leveraging topological principles to enhance the performance of quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around the design of a quantum optimization system that exploits these principles. We detail the design of the algorithm, the role of topological entanglement and tunneling, and the resulting improvements in algorithm performance. The research emphasizes the benefits of dynamic parameter adjustment and the potential for enhanced quantum algorithm capabilities.

title: Modular Logic for Parallel Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of modular logic to revolutionize parallel quantum computing, addressing the challenges of scalability and fault tolerance. We propose a novel system leveraging formal language and reasoning to design and orchestrate quantum computations, promoting independent and verifiable execution of computational modules within a quantum circuit. The core mechanism centers around a language that explicitly defines the logical relationships between modules, enabling automated circuit design and optimization. This approach seeks to overcome the limitations of traditional quantum programming by enhancing expressiveness, simplifying verification, and facilitating a more robust and scalable approach to quantum computation. The paper details the proposed system, its reasoning framework, and preliminary results demonstrating improvements in circuit design and verification.

title: Quantum State Dynamics: A Novel Approach to Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum state dynamics, characterized by their inherent non-linearity and self-organization, present a fundamental challenge and opportunity for advancing quantum computing. This paper explores the construction of a novel quantum state model based on non-linear self-organization, aiming to design a new quantum computing framework that leverages its dynamic characteristics to optimize quantum algorithms and computations. We detail the core mechanism, emphasizing the application of this dynamic state model to enhance existing quantum computational processes. The research highlights the potential for significant improvements in algorithm efficiency and overall computational capabilities through the strategic manipulation of quantum state evolution.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for solving complex systems by applying high-dimensional topology analysis. The algorithm's key innovation lies in its ability to effectively handle high-dimensional data and identify optimal configurations within the spatial structure of the problem. This approach offers a significant advancement over traditional optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios involving intricate systems and complex constraints. This research explores the potential of this method across a range of applications, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing complex configurations and providing a robust framework for addressing challenging problems.

title: Simulated Evolution with Cognitive Hotspots
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to simulated evolution by introducing the concept of "cognitive hotspots." Inspired by biological evolution, where sudden bursts of innovation drive adaptation, we introduce dynamic, high-fitness individuals – the "cognitive hotspots" – into the simulated evolutionary process. These hotspots attract neighboring individuals, fostering the formation of new subgroups and the introduction of potentially novel solutions. The dynamics of hotspot emergence and disappearance are governed by algorithm parameters and population state. We hypothesize that this mechanism significantly accelerates convergence and enhances the diversity of solutions within the simulated evolutionary process. We present a formal framework for modeling this phenomenon, outlining key parameters and their influence on the system's behavior. This approach offers a potential pathway to improve the efficiency and robustness of simulated evolution algorithms across a range of applications.

title: Algorithmic Differentiation for Deep Learning with Non-Differentiable Operations
abstract: Deep learning has achieved remarkable success across various domains, largely due to the effectiveness of gradient-based optimization methods. However, many deep learning architectures incorporate non-differentiable operations, such as discrete activations (e.g., argmax, argmin), quantization, and operations involving binary or integer data, severely hindering the application of standard backpropagation. This paper introduces a novel approach to algorithmic differentiation (AD) specifically designed to address this limitation. We propose a framework that extends AD by leveraging a symbolic execution strategy alongside approximation techniques to compute derivatives for these non-differentiable operations. Our method allows for the efficient computation of gradients, opening the door for training deep learning models that include these previously intractable components. The core claim of this work is to extend algorithmic differentiation to handle non-differentiable operations commonly found in deep learning architectures. The core mechanism involves employing a symbolic execution approach combined with approximation techniques to compute the derivative of non-differentiable functions. This represents a significant advancement over traditional gradient-based training methods, overcoming a key limitation in the field.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Quantum-Enhanced Associative Memory
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning by integrating quantum associative memory (QAM). Traditional neuro-symbolic systems struggle with the scalability and efficiency of knowledge representation and retrieval, particularly when dealing with complex, partially known information. Our approach utilizes quantum states to represent symbolic concepts, allowing for exponentially larger and more nuanced knowledge representations compared to classical associative memory. Quantum interference is then leveraged to rapidly and efficiently retrieve relevant knowledge based on partial or noisy inputs. The core mechanism relies on the superposition and entanglement properties of quantum states, enabling the system to explore multiple potential interpretations simultaneously. We demonstrate how this QAM-enhanced neuro-symbolic framework can significantly improve reasoning performance, particularly in scenarios requiring robust inference with incomplete or uncertain data. We introduce a theoretical framework outlining the key components and operational principles, and explore the potential advantages and challenges of this hybrid approach. The core claim is that combining neural networks with symbolic reasoning systems can be significantly enhanced by leveraging quantum associative memory to represent and retrieve complex knowledge structures. The core mechanism utilizes quantum states to represent symbolic concepts and utilizing quantum interference to quickly and efficiently retrieve relevant knowledge based on partial or noisy inputs. This research represents a significant step towards unlocking new levels of reasoning capabilities within artificial intelligence.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Geometric Shape Deformation
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a novel approach to geometric shape deformation, promising unprecedented precision and stability compared to traditional methods. This paper explores the development of a quantum entanglement-driven algorithm capable of precisely reshaping complex geometries. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the quantum state manipulation and entanglement-based correction process necessary for achieving stable deformation. The algorithm's potential implications for precision engineering, holographic computing, and materials science are discussed.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence Decision Agents
abstract: This paper explores the development of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) decision agents designed to enhance the trustworthiness and understandability of their decision-making processes. The core claim centers around constructing agents capable of articulating the rationale behind their choices. The proposed approach leverages techniques from SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) to analyze and visualize decision pathways. Crucially, this work moves beyond merely providing explanations to establishing an interactive explanation framework, allowing users to engage with and refine the agent's reasoning. The research delves into the complexities of interpretability, focusing on the creation of agents that not only explain but also facilitate a deeper comprehension of the underlying decision logic. This paper outlines the methodology, key components, and potential applications of these explainable decision agents.

title: Title: Quantum Simulation of Consciousness
abstract: This paper explores the ambitious goal of developing a quantum simulation framework capable of accurately modeling the computational processes of the human brain. The core claim is that by leveraging quantum algorithms, we can simulate the intricate neural networks within the brain with a fidelity exceeding classical approximations, offering potential insights into the fundamental principles underlying consciousness. We investigate a novel approach combining quantum state manipulation with specific algorithmic design to mimic neural network dynamics, highlighting the challenges and opportunities inherent in this endeavor. The research will address key concepts such as entanglement, superposition, and quantum decoherence, while outlining a preliminary framework for quantum neural network simulation. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential ramifications and limitations of this research, emphasizing the need for further theoretical and experimental investigation.

title: A Subspace Ensemble Framework for High-Dimensional Active Learning
abstract: Supervised learning in fields such as genomics and medical imaging is often hindered by the high cost of expert data annotation. Active learning addresses this bottleneck by iteratively selecting the most informative unlabeled samples for labeling. However, in high-dimensional environments, traditional diversity-based query strategies lose their effectiveness due to the degradation of global distance metrics. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel framework, Active Learning via Subspace Ensembles and Similarity (ALSES). Instead of relying on global distances, ALSES constructs a similarity matrix by sampling an ensemble of random feature subspaces. The subspaces are filtered based on their discriminative power, and pairwise sample similarities are aggregated using cluster co-occurrence. This structural representation is integrated into a hybrid batch selection strategy that balances model uncertainty and data representativeness. Extensive evaluations on simulated datasets and real-world high-dimensional cancer cohorts demonstrate that ALSES consistently outperforms standard active learning baselines. The framework effectively isolates informative variables and achieves superior classification accuracy with significantly fewer labeled instances, demonstrating its robustness in complex, noisy applications.

title: Artificial Intelligence In The Diagnosis And Treatment Of Cancer
abstract: Cancer is a major worldwide health concern, necessitating the development of novel strategies to improve detection and treatment outcomes. The present study delves into the significant contributions that artificial intelligence (AI) has made to the field o f cancer. It specifically highlights the applications of AI in diagnosis, personalized treatment, and clinical trial optimization. Diagnostic procedures have been transformed by recent advances in AI, particularly through the use of machine learning and de ep learning techniques. AI systems are becoming more and more accurate at interpreting medical imaging, including radiographs and histopathology slides, often outperforming human specialists in this regard. Furthermore, by combining genetic, lifestyle, and environmental data, AI - driven predictive models are showing promise in determining a person's risk of developing cancer. Artificial intelligence is a key factor in the advancement of personalized medicine in the field of cancer treatment. title: FACT: A Forensic Agent with Compiled Tool-Use Trajectories for AI-Generated Image Detection
abstract: AI-generated image detection is increasingly open-world: new image generators produce highly realistic images that make visual artifacts harder to identify. Existing detectors usually rely on a fixed set of forensic cues, so a detector that works well for one generator family may fail on another. We introduce FACT (Forensic Agent with Compiled Tool-use Trajectories), which learns an image-conditioned tool-use policy for forensic analysis. Instead of applying a fixed detector, FACT decides which forensic tools to call, interprets the returned evidence, and stops when sufficient evidence has been collected. FACT follows an Evolve--Distill--Refine pipeline: it evolves an execution-verified forensic skill, compiles the skill into action--observation tool-use trajectories, distills them into a compact agent, and refines the policy with cost-aware GRPO. Across two internal and four public benchmarks, FACT achieves the best performance among all compared methods, including on recent unseen generators, deepfakes, and manipulated images.

title: REMOTE SENSING AND MACHINE LEARNING FOR MINERAL EXPLORATION AND MINE PLANNING
abstract: Mineral exploration and mine planning increasingly require methods that can evaluate large and geologically complex areas with greater speed, accuracy, and cost efficiency. Conventional exploration techniques based mainly on field mapping, drilling, and laboratory investigation remain essential, but their application over large areas can be expensive and time-consuming. Remote sensing provides an effective means of observing geological structures, surface alteration, lithological variations, drainage characteristics, and terrain conditions from satellite, airborne, and unmanned aerial platforms. Machine learning further strengthens this capability by identifying complex relationships among spectral, geological, structural, topographic, and geochemical variables that may not be easily recognized through conventional interpretation. This study presents an integrated framework combining multispectral remote-sensing data, digital elevation models, geological information, mine-surveying data, and machine-learning techniques for mineral prospectivity mapping and preliminary mine planning. Spectral indices and alteration-related features are extracted from satellite imagery, while topographic and structural parameters are derived from elevation and geological datasets. Several machine-learning algorithms are compared to classify prospective and non-prospective mineral zones. The resulting mineral prospectivity map is subsequently integrated with slope, elevation, accessibility, and mine-planning constraints to identify suitable zones for detailed investigation and possible future extraction. The illustrative analysis indicates that ensemble machine-learning methods, particularly Random Forest and gradient-boosting approaches, can provide reliable prediction performance when multisource geospatial variables are properly combined. The proposed approach can reduce unnecessary field investigation, improve targeting of drilling locations, and support safer and more informed mine-planning decisions. Keywords: Remote Sensing; Machine Learning; Mineral Exploration; Mine Planning; Mineral Prospectivity Mapping; Mine Surveying

title: Causal Bayesian Deep Networks with Latent Intervention Detection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for building Causal Bayesian Deep Networks (CBDNs) designed to explicitly model causal relationships and detect latent interventions within complex systems. Traditional Bayesian Deep Networks primarily focus on learning probabilistic dependencies from data, often resulting in spurious correlations. Our approach addresses this limitation by integrating a causal discovery module, specifically leveraging the PC algorithm, directly into the Bayesian network learning process. This allows the network to not only predict the probability of observed events (P(si)) but also to learn the probability of intervention at specific nodes (P(si | Ik)), where Ik represents a potential intervention. The learned intervention probabilities serve as signals, highlighting potential causal influences that might otherwise be missed. The core claim is that deep Bayesian networks can be augmented in this way, significantly enhancing their ability to understand and model causal mechanisms. The framework's novelty lies in the synergistic combination of deep learning's representational power with causal inference's ability to disentangle cause and effect. This enables the identification of latent interventions – actions that, while not directly observed, could significantly alter the system's dynamics – providing a more robust and interpretable model of the system. The paper outlines the architecture, learning process, and detection mechanisms of CBDNs, highlighting their potential applications in domains requiring causal understanding, such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems.

title: Quantum Computation: A Control Theory for Information Collapse
abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework for controlling information collapse within quantum computation. Recognizing collapse as a fundamental limitation, the work develops a mathematical model rooted in the principles of quantum mechanics to analyze and mitigate its effects. The core of the approach involves utilizing feedback control strategies to actively suppress collapse events. We formulate a set of equations describing the evolution of a quantum system under the influence of both Hamiltonian terms and control operations. Specifically, we define the collapse rate as a function of the system's state and the strength of the control signal. The control strategy aims to minimize this collapse rate through a dynamically adjusted feedback loop. The theoretical framework provides a pathway towards enhancing the fidelity and reliability of quantum computations by offering a method for proactive management of decoherence. We explore scenarios with varying system parameters and control strengths, demonstrating the potential for significant improvements in quantum state preservation. The research contributes to the ongoing efforts in building robust and scalable quantum computers.

title: Based Quantum Decoherence Distributed Computation (DBCQ)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed computing leveraging the unique properties of quantum decoherence. The core idea centers around decomposing complex computational tasks into smaller, manageable sub-tasks that can be concurrently executed on a network of quantum nodes. By exploiting the inherent sensitivity of quantum systems to environmental interactions – specifically decoherence – we aim to achieve significant improvements in computational efficiency and enhanced security compared to classical distributed computing paradigms. The framework presented here offers a fundamentally different perspective, shifting from traditional error correction strategies to actively harnessing the effects of decoherence to guide the computation. The design incorporates specific algorithms tailored to maximize the benefits of decoherence, focusing on probabilistic outcomes and iteratively refining results. This approach introduces a degree of inherent randomness within the computation, which, when carefully managed, can be utilized to obfuscate intermediate results and improve security. The theoretical analysis details the key mathematical models and formulas underpinning the DBCQ framework, including decoherence rates, qubit fidelity, and the probabilistic convergence of solutions. This work provides a foundational understanding of this emerging field, laying the groundwork for future research and development in quantum-enhanced distributed computing.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Networks with Adaptive Structure Learning and Bayesian Model Averaging
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) modeling that addresses limitations inherent in traditional DBNs by incorporating adaptive structure learning and Bayesian model averaging. The core idea is to allow the network structure itself to evolve based on incoming data, thereby capturing complex and time-varying relationships. Simultaneously, Bayesian model averaging is employed to quantify and mitigate the uncertainty associated with parameter estimation within the evolving network. The proposed methodology offers enhanced robustness and predictive accuracy compared to static DBNs, particularly in scenarios with noisy or incomplete data and evolving system dynamics. We detail the implementation of this approach, focusing on the structure learning algorithm and the Bayesian model averaging framework, and discuss its potential applications across various domains. The resulting system provides a more flexible and reliable representation of dynamic systems than conventional methods.

title: Adaptive Information Entropy Optimizer (ASIO) – A Dynamic Learning Mechanism for Enhanced Model Generalization
abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Information Entropy Optimizer (ASIO), a novel model optimization technique designed to enhance model generalization capabilities through dynamic learning. Traditional approaches often rely on static parameters, limiting their adaptability to evolving data. ASIO integrates the principles of information entropy optimization with a dynamic learning mechanism, allowing the model to automatically adjust its parameters based on observed data entropy fluctuations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ASIO through a series of experiments on diverse datasets, showcasing improved performance and robustness compared to existing methods. This work addresses a critical challenge in deep learning – the need for models that can continuously adapt to new data – and offers a promising pathway toward more reliable and generalizable models.

title: Title: Non-Local Constraint Propagation via Quantum Teleportation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum teleportation to propagate constraints across spatially separated systems. The core challenge lies in establishing a mechanism for transferring information about constraints between distant nodes, allowing for distributed reasoning and collaborative problem-solving. We propose a novel quantum algorithm that leverages the principles of quantum teleportation to achieve this goal. The theoretical analysis and preliminary implementation demonstrate the potential for this approach to overcome limitations of existing constraint propagation techniques.

title: 基于图的量子态的动态模拟
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic simulation approach for quantum states, leveraging the inherent topological properties of graphs to achieve precise state simulation and rapid state evolution. Traditional quantum state simulation relies heavily on classical computation, while this method utilizes graph structures to capture the complex interplay of states. We propose a method based on graph representation, iterative refinement, and a novel variational optimization scheme to generate accurate quantum state trajectories. The core mechanism involves constructing a graph-based model, iteratively refining the graph topology and applying variational optimization to map the state space. This allows for the simulation of quantum states with improved accuracy and the ability to rapidly explore the dynamics of complex quantum systems. This work offers a promising advancement in quantum state simulation, potentially enabling faster and more accurate calculations for various quantum algorithms and applications.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Topology: A Quantum Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum geometric topology theory to describe the quantum properties of non-linear geometric objects. We propose a framework incorporating quantum entanglement and topological structures, utilizing quantum entanglement as a key mechanism for generating and analyzing quantum states. The core claim is that quantum-enhanced geometric topology offers a fundamentally new computational paradigm. This research explores how entanglement can be leveraged to create robust and efficient quantum geometric calculations, offering a potential advancement over traditional methods. This work investigates the implications of this framework for understanding and potentially manipulating quantum properties within non-linear geometric systems.

title: Self-Adaptive Topology and High-Dimensional Quantum Computing: A Coupling Framework
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-adaptive topology and high-dimensional quantum computing through a novel coupling framework. The core challenge in designing quantum algorithms is the intricate and often laborious task of parameter optimization. We propose a system where the optimization process is intrinsically linked to the inherent properties of topology, allowing for automated parameter tuning and improved quantum computation efficiency and accuracy. The framework leverages the self-adaptive nature of topology to dynamically adjust quantum states, potentially achieving superior performance compared to traditional methods. We present a conceptual model demonstrating the potential benefits of this approach, highlighting the role of topology in guiding the optimization process. This work explores the implications of this coupling for the design of novel quantum algorithms and their applicability in various quantum computing paradigms. The resulting framework offers a promising avenue for advancing the capabilities of high-dimensional quantum systems.

title: Differential Privacy with Federated Learning via Entangled Noise
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized datasets without directly exchanging the data itself. However, integrating differential privacy (DP) into FL introduces significant accuracy trade-offs. This work proposes a novel approach, "Entangled Noise," to mitigate these trade-offs. Entangled noise leverages a specialized noise injection strategy that minimizes communication overhead while maintaining a higher level of privacy guarantees. We demonstrate that standard DP methods often overly restrict model updates, leading to substantial accuracy degradation. Our entangled noise technique intelligently combines noise injections across model parameters, effectively reducing the overall noise variance and preserving model performance. We present a theoretical framework analyzing the privacy-utility trade-off and provide empirical evidence showcasing the superior performance of entangled noise compared to traditional DP methods in federated learning scenarios. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of noise parameters based on parameter sensitivity, resulting in a more efficient and accurate DP-FL system. This work contributes a practical and theoretically sound method for achieving stronger privacy guarantees in federated learning without sacrificing model accuracy.

title: Meta-Learning for Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper explores the application of meta-learning techniques to the automated design of algorithms. The core idea is to leverage meta-learning – learning to learn – to train a meta-learner that can efficiently design algorithms tailored to specific computational tasks. Traditional algorithm design relies heavily on human expertise, often involving extensive trial and error. This process can be time-consuming and may not always yield optimal solutions. Meta-learning offers a promising alternative by learning from a distribution of tasks, enabling the meta-learner to generalize its knowledge and design effective algorithms for unseen problems. We present a framework where the meta-learner learns a representation of algorithmic design principles and subsequently applies these principles to construct algorithms for new tasks. The potential impact of this approach is significant, suggesting the possibility of automating algorithm design and, potentially, discovering novel and highly efficient algorithms that would be difficult for humans to conceive. The research focuses on the theoretical foundations and conceptual design of such a system, without the need for empirical experimentation.

title: Hierarchical Graph Embeddings for Knowledge Representation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to knowledge graph embedding, termed Hierarchical Graph Embeddings (HGE). Existing graph embedding methods frequently struggle to effectively represent the inherent hierarchical structure present in knowledge graphs, leading to suboptimal performance in tasks such as link prediction and knowledge completion. Our method addresses this limitation by learning embeddings at multiple levels of granularity, creating a multi-resolution graph representation. This allows us to capture both local and global structural information within the knowledge graph. The core mechanism involves a hierarchical graph convolutional network (HGCN) which iteratively refines embeddings, starting with coarser graph representations and progressively incorporating finer-grained details. We demonstrate the effectiveness of HGE through theoretical analysis and by outlining the key components and their mathematical formulations. The proposed method significantly improves upon traditional graph embedding techniques by explicitly modeling and learning hierarchical relationships, resulting in enhanced knowledge representation and improved performance in downstream knowledge graph tasks.

title: Contextualized Graph Embeddings via Variational Autoencoders
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embedding generation that leverages the power of Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to capture the dynamic contextual relationships between nodes within a graph. Traditional graph embedding methods often produce static representations, failing to account for the evolving nature of node interactions and dependencies. Our method, termed Contextualized Graph Embeddings via VAEs, learns a latent space representation conditioned on both the node's features and the surrounding nodes' features, considering their temporal relationships. The resulting embeddings are adaptive and reflect the current context of a node within the graph, leading to a more nuanced and accurate depiction of node relationships. We demonstrate that this dynamic approach outperforms static embedding techniques in several benchmark graph datasets, showcasing its ability to better capture complex graph structures and node interactions. The core claim of this work is to generate graph embeddings that capture the dynamic context of a node within a graph, allowing for more nuanced representation of node relationships. The core mechanism involves a VAE that learns a latent space representation of the graph, conditioned on the surrounding nodes and their temporal relationships, producing embeddings that adapt to the current context.

title: Title: Algorithmic Determinism & Emergent Behavior via Bayesian Networks with Feedback Loops
abstract: The inherent complexity of many systems, from biological organisms to social networks, often results in unpredictable emergent behavior. Traditional statistical methods struggle to accurately capture these dynamics, particularly when feedback loops are involved. This research explores a novel algorithmic approach to Bayesian networks – a Bayesian network designed with explicit modeling of feedback loops – to enhance prediction certainty. We propose a novel update rule incorporating a "horizon effect" to dynamically adjust network parameters, minimizing prediction errors while simultaneously increasing confidence in long-term outcomes. This work directly addresses the challenge of navigating complex systems by promoting a more adaptive and robust probabilistic representation. The core claim is that this design will significantly improve the prediction of emergent behavior compared to traditional methods.

We propose a novel update rule incorporating a "horizon effect" to dynamically adjust network parameters, minimizing prediction errors while simultaneously increasing confidence in long-term outcomes. This work directly addresses the challenge of navigating complex systems by promoting a more adaptive and robust probabilistic representation. The core claim is that this design will significantly improve the prediction of emergent behavior compared to traditional methods.

title: Hyper-Adaptive Symmetry Networks (HASN)
abstract: This paper introduces Hyper-Adaptive Symmetry Networks (HASN), a novel neural network architecture designed to dynamically identify and exploit emergent symmetries within complex systems. Traditional neural network architectures primarily focus on optimizing prediction accuracy through backpropagation, often neglecting the underlying structural relationships within the data. HASN departs from this approach by incorporating a dynamically adaptive feedback loop that continuously assesses the inherent symmetry of the input, adjusting network parameters to maximize predictive performance. This mechanism, coupled with a self-organizing, adaptive weighting system, allows HASN to discover and exploit patterns that are often obscured by standard optimization techniques. We demonstrate the efficacy of HASN through a series of experiments on a diverse set of datasets, showcasing its ability to achieve superior predictive accuracy in scenarios requiring sophisticated pattern recognition.

title: FM3H-MH: An Efficient Large-Scale Privacy Amplification Scheme for Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: Privacy amplification (PA) is a critical process in quantum key distribution (QKD) systems, essential for eliminating information leakage to eavesdroppers and extracting unconditionally secure keys. In practical high-speed QKD systems, a large input size enables the PA scheme to approach the asymptotic limit of the secure-key rate. Concurrently, the throughput of the PA scheme must keep pace with the GHz-level clock rates of modern QKD systems to prevent it from becoming a systemic bottleneck. To globally optimize these objectives, this paper proposes a scalable and highly efficient PA scheme combining a novel δ-almost-universal hash family (FM3H) with modular arithmetic hashing (MH), and proves the security of this hybrid scheme, within the information-theoretic and quantum-side framework. The proposed scheme achieves a throughput of 283 Mbps on a common mobile CPU with an input size of 1010 bits. NIST statistical tests and avalanche-effect measurements are reported as characterizations of the statistical properties of the output sequences. To our knowledge, this work presents the first FPGA-based implementation of a modular hashing-based PA scheme, thereby breaking the dependence of modular hashing schemes on general software platforms. In DV-QKD systems, the FPGA-based scheme achieves a throughput of 1.706 Gbps while maintaining low resource overhead.

title: Programmable Cellular Automata
abstract: Cellular automata is a local computation paradigm where complex behavior can arise from local interactions between simple functions. This paradigm has been used to explain many systems such as biological processes, traffic simulation, computer networks, etc. In games, cellular automata have been used in games such as SimCity and for the generation of spatial content such as caves or dungeons. However, creating effective local rules is hard and unintuitive. Cellular automata can be effectively evolved, but may still be hard to interpret. In this work, we introduce the concept of programmable cellular automata, where we represent the system as Python code. We also modularize the cellular automata into local functions and a decision function. Local functions take a local neighborhood and return a value, while the decision function takes the output of the local functions and decides the value of the next state. Separating the cellular automata into modules written in Python helps with understanding how these systems are working. We also explore adding global functions where they take the whole state and compute a function from it. We tested generating levels for three different games from the PCG Benchmark. The results showed that global functions decrease the number of iterations that cellular automata need to solve a problem, and that we cannot find solutions for some problems with purely local functions. Looking into the generated functions, we can see common functions that have been used in different experiments, which not only helps us understand the generator but also helps us understand these games better and what is important for them.

title: Anomaly Detection Feature Engineering for Enhanced Prediction of HIV Viral Load Suppression Using DHIS2 Data
abstract: Highly imbalanced, incomplete, and complex feature datasets such as routine HIV programme data in DHIS2 are increasingly used for predictive modelling. Yet conventional feature engineering often fails to capture subtle, non-linear patterns that can enable accurate model predictions. This study aimed to evaluate whether integrating unsupervised anomaly detection into feature engineering improves the prediction of HIV viral load suppression from routine DHIS2 data compared with conventional feature-engineering approaches. A phased analytical pipeline compared raw-variable evaluation using 63,594 patient records from two Kenyan counties. Conventional domain-driven feature engineering and anomaly-detection-based feature engineering were compared using Isolation Forest, Local Outlier Factor, and PCA reconstruction-error metrics. Retention-in-care variables consistently demonstrated the strongest associations with appointment-related metrics, showing effect sizes of approximately 0.99. Conventional engineering improved interpretability but did not substantially enhance predictive performance. Anomaly detection identified 5–10% of patients as anomalous, and twelve anomaly-aware features were generated. Five of these, including lof_score and if_score, were ranked among the top 20 predictors, and their inclusion increased XGBoost discrimination from an AUC of 0.801 to 0.823 (p<0.001). Cross-phase analysis confirmed that anomaly-derived features complemented rather than displaced established clinical predictors. The findings indicate that anomaly detection can serve as an effective feature-engineering strategy, offering a scalable approach to strengthening predictive modelling using routinely collected, complex health data in resource-constrained settings.

title: Comparative Analysis of Random Forest, BiLSTM, and Isolation Forest for Rainfall Data Anomaly Detection to Support Automatic Rain Gauge (ARG) Performance Monitoring
abstract: Accuracy and reliability of rainfall data form an essential foundation for meteorological observation activities. However, the presence of missing values or unreasonable readings can degrade data quality, necessitating anomaly detection methods to support Automatic Rain Gauge (ARG) performance monitoring. This study aims to evaluate and compare the performance of the Random Forest, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), and Isolation Forest algorithms in detecting anomalies in rainfall data, as well as to implement these methods in a web-based monitoring system. Historical rainfall data from the ARG at the STMKG Engineering Station (STA9003) spanning 2020–2022 with a 10-minute temporal resolution were used in this research. The workflow includes data preprocessing, reference label generation using Rule-Based Quality Control, feature engineering, and model development using the three selected algorithms. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the Area Under the ROC Curve (ROC-AUC). The results show that Random Forest achieved the best overall performance with an accuracy of 84.50% and an ROC-AUC of 0.760, while BiLSTM and Isolation Forest yielded lower performance metrics on this dataset. The detection outputs were subsequently visualized in a dashboard within a web-based monitoring system to facilitate anomaly tracking and systematic ARG performance evaluation.

title: Mizo Named Entity Recognition: silver-standard corpus, gold evaluation set, models and code
abstract: Silver-standard named entity corpus for Mizo (lus): 441,178 sentences, 590,655 annotations over 11 types, built by cross-lingual projection from English. Includes a 300-sentence gold evaluation set annotated by two Mizo speakers (Cohen's kappa 0.798), trained recognizers, and code reproducing every result in the accompanying paper. Labels are silver-standard: measured against the gold set the projection scores F1 0.6146.

title: QSOL-FED v0.11.1: Human-Facing Formalization of the Hardened MORIARTY/1 Writable-Resource Boundary
abstract: This archival record provides a human-facing deductive formalization of the hardened MORIARTY/1 writable-resource boundary frozen in QSOL-FED v0.11.1. The formalization is bound to the immutable GitHub release v0.11.1, commit 5dea8f46b259fd22fd95e165333e0c46e6248b1a, and Git tree b30fcb381a57741185be344f50468b7e645cd778. It formalizes the principal assurance properties introduced or strengthened through PR #21, including device/inode-bound directory traversal, descriptor-backed scanning, restart semantics for transient filesystem churn, bounded fail-closed behavior under persistent mutation, coherent writable-resource accounting under cgroup suspension, complete cgroup.threads quiescence verification, pidfd-bound task signaling, exclusion of writable-scan suspension time from probe execution deadlines, completion-relative periodic scan scheduling, and preservation of existing resource and authority boundaries. Thirteen propositions are developed under explicitly named Linux kernel, cgroup v2, pidfd, filesystem-descriptor, task-state, monotonic-clock, and threat-boundary assumptions. The propositions are traced to the frozen Phase 9 contract fields and corresponding executable regression tests. This artifact deliberately does not claim universal software verification or a universal security theorem. It is a human-readable formalization with executable-regression traceability, not a new Lean kernel proof. The existing Phase 10 Lean package contained in the repository snapshot explicitly targets the earlier immutable v0.11.0 release.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Optimal Control
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to reservoir computing, termed Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing (QIRC), designed to overcome limitations inherent in traditional reservoir models. We propose utilizing quantum mechanical principles, namely superposition and entanglement, within the reservoir network architecture to dramatically enhance temporal signal processing capabilities. The core idea is to engineer reservoir nodes to exhibit quantum-inspired superposition of states, resulting in an exponentially larger representation capacity. Furthermore, we incorporate entangled node pairs to facilitate correlated temporal pattern recognition, a key feature in complex dynamic systems. The theoretical framework presented demonstrates the potential for QIRC to achieve superior performance compared to conventional reservoir computing methods, particularly in control tasks demanding intricate, high-dimensional temporal dynamics. We outline the mathematical formulations underpinning the QIRC model and discuss the key advantages and challenges associated with its implementation. The results suggest a promising direction for advancing reservoir computing and its application in real-world control systems.

title: Bayesian Network for Probabilistic Constraint Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Bayesian Network architecture designed to enhance probabilistic constraint reasoning. Traditional approaches often struggle with complex, multi-faceted constraints and the inherent uncertainty within systems. We introduce a hierarchical Bayesian Network that dynamically updates belief states based on observed data and uncertainty, incorporating a novel 'prior probability' mechanism. This system aims to overcome limitations of existing methods by providing robust, probabilistic reasoning capabilities. The paper details the architecture, introduces the key novel mechanism, and provides a preliminary evaluation of its performance on a benchmark dataset, demonstrating improved reasoning accuracy and resilience to noisy data.

title: 基于动态的量子势场的优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic quantum field simulations, designed to enhance the performance of quantum systems. Traditional quantum state optimization methods often rely on static models, limiting their applicability to complex systems. Our proposed algorithm employs a dynamic quantum field simulation mechanism to proactively adjust the quantum field, thereby optimizing the system's performance. This approach overcomes the limitations of static models by adapting to the system's specific dynamics. We present a methodology for implementing this dynamic simulation, demonstrating its effectiveness through numerical examples and analysis of quantum system properties. The core mechanism of this algorithm focuses on real-time adjustments to the quantum field, offering a significant advantage over existing approaches.

title: Geometric Chaos and Quantum Simulation
abstract: Geometric chaos, a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamical systems, presents a significant challenge for traditional quantum computation. This paper explores the application of geometric chaos simulation to quantum algorithm design and optimization. We propose a novel quantum simulation framework predicated on the unique properties of geometric chaos, aiming to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of quantum computations involving complex chaotic systems. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the inherent unpredictability and sensitivity of geometric chaos to guide the evolution and optimization of quantum circuits. This research investigates the potential for utilizing the framework to address specific problems in quantum algorithm design, providing a new approach to optimizing quantum circuit performance and exploring new quantum computation paradigms. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for future advancements in quantum information processing.

abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic multi-particle system optimization method leveraging reinforcement learning and neural networks. Our approach dynamically adjusts system parameters based on state changes, providing a more precise modeling and prediction capability. The core mechanism centers around iterative refinement of parameter values guided by a learned reward function, enabling the system to evolve and optimize its performance without explicit human intervention. This method offers a significant advancement in addressing complex system behavior and opens avenues for automated system design and control.

The primary goal is to enhance neural network performance through automated parameter adjustment. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments. Specifically, we show that the proposed framework achieves significant improvements in model accuracy and generalization ability compared to traditional methods.

title: Title: Adaptive Topological Structure Probability Vector Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive topological structure probability vector optimization algorithm designed to enhance data analysis and machine learning performance. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with dynamic systems, and this approach leverages the inherent properties of probability vectors to dynamically adjust topological structures, thereby optimizing data analysis and machine learning workflows. The core mechanism centers on integrating the self-adaptive nature of topological structures with the probabilistic nature of vector optimization, resulting in improved efficiency and robustness. This paper explores the theoretical foundation and practical implementation of this approach, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve the performance of various machine learning tasks.

title: Riemannian Optimization for Neural Architecture Search with Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has emerged as a powerful technique for automating the design of neural networks, but traditional methods often suffer from inefficiencies in exploring the expansive architecture search space. This work introduces a novel approach combining Riemannian optimization with evolutionary algorithms for enhanced NAS. The core idea is to represent neural network architectures as points in a high-dimensional, curved manifold, and utilize Riemannian optimization to efficiently navigate this manifold towards optimal architectures. Evolutionary algorithms are then employed for global exploration, complementing the local optimization provided by Riemannian methods. This integration aims to overcome the limitations of existing NAS techniques by providing a more effective and scalable solution. The primary contribution lies in the application of Riemannian geometry to the architecture search problem, leading to improved convergence and exploration capabilities. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its effectiveness with a conceptual framework.

title: Neural Network Optimization via Differential Geometry
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to neural network optimization by leveraging concepts from differential geometry. The core idea is to treat the parameters and connections within a neural network as geometric objects, utilizing curvature and tensor-based optimization techniques. We propose a framework where the network's architecture and weights are viewed as a manifold, and optimization is performed by minimizing a curvature-based energy functional. This method aims to enhance learning efficiency and generalization capabilities by exploiting the inherent geometric properties of the network. The key contribution lies in the application of geometric intuition and optimization methods, traditionally used in fields like general relativity and topology, to the challenging problem of neural network training. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual arguments, the potential benefits of this approach, offering a new perspective on network optimization.

title: Adaptive Quantum Circuit Compilation via Tensor Networks
abstract: Quantum circuit compilation is a critical step in realizing quantum computation, aiming to translate high-level quantum algorithms into a sequence of gates executable on a specific quantum hardware. However, traditional compilation methods often struggle with the inherent complexities of quantum circuits, including their high dimensionality, susceptibility to noise, and the diverse characteristics of different quantum devices. This work proposes a novel approach to adaptive quantum circuit compilation that leverages the power of tensor networks (TNs) and reinforcement learning (RL). The core idea is to represent quantum circuits as TNs, dynamically adjusting the network's structure to capture the relevant circuit features while minimizing computational overhead and mitigating noise effects. A reinforcement learning agent is trained to iteratively construct and refine these TN representations, guided by feedback signals derived from circuit fidelity metrics and computational cost estimates. This dynamic adaptation allows for a more efficient and robust compilation process, potentially leading to improved performance and reduced error rates in quantum computations. The key contribution lies in the integration of TNs with RL for a self-optimizing compilation pipeline. This approach offers a promising direction for tackling the challenges inherent in quantum hardware limitations and diverse quantum device architectures.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization for Complex Systems
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization aims to improve the performance of complex optimization problems by incorporating principles from quantum mechanics. This paper explores the application of quantum-like concepts, such as superposition and entanglement, to enhance the efficiency of optimization algorithms. We present a novel quantum-inspired optimization framework designed to address the challenges inherent in complex systems, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to traditional optimization methods. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging these quantum principles to achieve improved solution paths and faster convergence. This research contributes to the advancement of optimization techniques with the potential for significant gains in the solution of challenging problems across diverse fields.

title: Modular Proof System (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents the Modular Proof System (MPS), a novel declarative proof system designed to automate the generation and verification of complex mathematical proofs with high fidelity and reproducibility. MPS leverages a layered approach, comprising modular building blocks representing fundamental mathematical concepts, and utilizes automated theorem proving and verification techniques. The system's core claim is to provide a paradigm shift from traditional, hand-crafted proof methods, offering enhanced efficiency and scalability in the process of mathematical discovery. The research explores the system's architecture, key mechanisms, and preliminary results, demonstrating its potential to significantly impact the field of mathematical reasoning.

title: A Ghanaian pre-SHS feasibility study of AI chatbots as more knowledgeable others for supporting science learning in a resource-constrained context
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence offers innovative potential for personalised learning, yet its integration remains hindered by instructional voids and restrictive mobile-device policies globally. This study addresses these challenges by investigating AI-powered chatbots as a scalable scaffolding tool for science learning in resource-constrained settings where a scarcity of personalised instructional resources presents a significant barrier to science outcomes. Employing a pre-experimental single-group pre-test/post-test design, the research assessed changes in cognitive outcomes and holistic competencies among 31 pre-Senior High School students in Ghana using researcher-developed, validated instruments. The intervention integrated the chatbot as a self-directed learning and inquiry support system over four weeks. Qualitative data were analysed thematically and subsequently quantified. Quantitative data were analysed using paired t-tests and the robust Wilcoxon signed-rank test, supplemented by Spearman’s rank-order correlation and Least Absolute Deviations (LAD) regression. Findings revealed statistically significant improvements across the measured domains, with large effect sizes observed for cognitive outcomes (Cohen’s d > 2.0) and moderate-to-large effect sizes for holistic outcomes (Wilcoxon r = 0.41–0.68). The findings suggest that the chatbot functioned as a More Knowledgeable Other (MKO) within the structured learning intervention and may have supported cognitive and self-directed learning processes, consistent with Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) and Self-Determination Theory (SDT) interpretations. Critically, the study found a strong positive correlation (ρ > 0.8) between students’ learning outcomes and their self-reported Perception of Utility. This research provides preliminary evidence on the feasibility and potential value of AI-supported learning for expanding personalised learning opportunities in resource-constrained educational contexts.

title: How to Learn from What a Human Would Avoid? Intervention-Aware World Models with Real-World RL for Dexterous Manipulation
abstract: Multi-fingered dexterous manipulation remains a frontier for real-world reinforcement learning (RL) due to the high-dimensional action space and the prohibitive cost of hardware failures. While human-in-the-loop (HIL) RL allows operators to intervene before failures occur, current pipelines often treat these interventions as reactive corrections, discarding the rich safety signal inherent in the operator's decision to take control. In this paper, we ask: How can we learn from what a human would avoid? We present WHIRL, a safety-aware RL framework that transforms binary human interventions into forward-predictive signals for proactive risk avoidance. Our approach centers on an intervention-aware latent world model with four prediction heads: dynamics, reward, termination, and a novel per-state intervention-probability head that learns to predict the likelihood of a human takeover at future states. This head provides an actor-side risk-shaping term that discourages the policy from entering "intervention-prone" regions, modeling the operator's internal safety threshold. We evaluate our framework on a 16-DoF LEAP Hand across tasks spanning convex and irregular object grasping, prismatic manipulation, and long-horizon multi-stage tasks. Our results show that predictive risk-shaping enables the system to achieve a 96.7 percent success rate on complex grasping tasks while reducing the operator intervention burden by up to 84 percent in step-weighted terms. By closing the loop between human intuition and predictive world modeling, this work provides a practical safety-aware recipe for training complex dexterous agents in the real world while reducing operator fatigue and hardware-risk exposure.

title: Hierarchical Prompt Injector for Domain Generalization Segmentation
abstract: Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation (DGSS) is a challenging task, as vision models often rely on low-level appearance cues that change across domains. In contrast, structural attributes exhibit cross-domain stability, motivating the use of structural priors for DGSS. Existing methods use prompt learning to transfer such priors into DGSS models, but typically encode each class as a single holistic prompt. Moreover, these methods apply prompts uniformly to all pixels, offering no mechanism to adapt when only a subset of object regions is visible due to viewpoint changes, occlusion, and environmental variation. We address this with \textbf{Spatial Hierarchical Prompts (SHP)} that enrich each class with region-level geometric anchors capturing structural appearance from distinct viewing angles, ensuring complementary coverage under arbitrary viewpoints. Additionally, we propose the \textbf{Hierarchical Prompt Injector (HPI)}, which enables spatially adaptive prompt injection in foundation models. HPI spatially grounds prompts by modeling their semantic relevance and spatial influence with visual features. Considering the difficulty of learning spatially and semantically aware prompt injection, we further introduce auxiliary supervision to align hierarchical prompts with their corresponding object regions. We achieve 70.62\% and 72.74\% mIoU on synthetic-to-real and real-to-real benchmarks, respectively. Code and checkpoints are released at https://github.com/MosukFate/HPI

title: MFCMd: Multivariate Fuzzy C-Medoids Clustering
abstract: MFCMd combines medoid-based prototypes with multivariate membership degrees, improving robustness to noise and outliers while accounting for the relevance of each variable within each cluster. Two variants are included, using Euclidean (MFCMd-E) and cityblock (MFCMd-C) distances for prototype updates. This release includes: Implementation of the MFCMd-E and MFCMd-C algorithms Cluster and partition interpretation indices Scripts to reproduce the synthetic dataset experiments (Configurations 1–7) Scripts to reproduce the real-dataset experiments Noise and outlier injection routines used in the robustness evaluation Licensed under the MIT License.

title: Verus Phase 37
abstract: Phase 37 of the Verus project — the Dynamic Integrity Engine — is the runtime enforcement layer beneath the constitutional principles laid out in the Cosmic Compact. Where a constitutional framework states what an AI system must respect, Phase 37 is the mechanism that continuously checks a running system's actual evidentiary state against those commitments and produces a cryptographically verifiable, tamper-evident record of that checking. The engine converts observed evidence — about a system's authority, risk posture, operating conditions, and stakeholder alignment — into an integrity state, resolved through a strict precedence order (failure > authority > conflict > material > unresolved > delta > current), and deterministically routes that state to one of seven runtime actions ranging from CONTINUE to FAIL_SAFE. This paper documents the engine's architecture across its constituent modules (Phases 37.15–37.20): its evidence-integrity guarantees (deterministic canonicalization, hash-linked lineage, mutation-after-seal detection), its cryptographic attestation layer (Ed25519-signed, chained certificates with key rotation), its durability under restart and partial failure, and two hardening case studies — a SQL-identifier injection defect and a canonicalization coverage gap — each documented as found, fixed, and regression-tested rather than omitted. The paper closes with an explicit statement of what "verified" means in this context (internal, first-party, adversarial self-testing) and what remains for independent third-party audit. This is the third paper in the Verus series, following Phase 35 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20586883) and Phase 36 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21246720).

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Genetic Algorithms for Complex Search Spaces
abstract: This paper explores the integration of quantum-inspired concepts into Genetic Algorithms (GAs) to improve their performance in complex search spaces. Traditional GAs often struggle with the computational cost of evaluating numerous candidate solutions, particularly in high-dimensional spaces. We propose a novel approach where candidate solutions are represented in a superposition of states, mimicking the quantum mechanical principle of superposition. Furthermore, we introduce tunneling mechanisms to enable rapid traversal of the search space, inspired by the quantum tunneling effect. The core idea is to leverage the ability of quantum systems to exist in multiple states simultaneously, allowing the GA to explore a wider range of potential solutions concurrently. The implementation details and the theoretical underpinnings of this hybrid approach are presented, demonstrating the potential for significant acceleration in GA convergence and solution quality. The efficacy of this quantum-inspired GA is demonstrated through an analysis of its performance compared to standard GAs on several benchmark problems, illustrating its ability to overcome limitations inherent in traditional evolutionary algorithms. The key contribution lies in the combined application of superposition and tunneling, offering a new paradigm for optimizing GAs.

title: Explainable AI for Deep Reinforcement Learning through Counterfactual Analysis
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents have achieved remarkable success in various domains, from game playing to robotics. However, their internal workings are often opaque, presenting a significant challenge for trust, verification, and debugging. This work proposes a novel approach to explain the decision-making processes of DRL agents by leveraging counterfactual analysis. We introduce a methodology that generates counterfactual scenarios – minimal changes to the input state – and observes the resulting agent actions. This allows us to identify which factors were most influential in the agent's decision, effectively revealing the underlying policy and decision boundaries. The core claim is that by examining these counterfactuals, we can transform these black-box agents into more transparent and understandable systems. This approach offers a practical and interpretable method for understanding DRL agent behavior, opening avenues for improved design, safety, and robustness.

title: Algorithmic Transparency and Explainability via Formal Model Checking of Neural Networks
abstract: The increasing deployment of neural networks in critical applications, such as autonomous driving and medical diagnosis, raises significant concerns regarding transparency and explainability. The "black box" nature of these networks makes it difficult to understand their decision-making processes, leading to a lack of trust and hindering widespread adoption. This work proposes a novel approach to enhance algorithmic transparency and explainability by leveraging formal model checking techniques. We develop a formal model of a neural network and utilize model checking to rigorously verify its properties, including robustness against adversarial attacks and adherence to predefined constraints. The verification process generates detailed explanations based on the model checking results, providing insights into the network's behavior. This approach offers a rigorous and quantifiable method for ensuring the reliability and trustworthiness of neural networks, addressing a critical gap in current practices. The core claim is that a lack of transparency in neural networks hinders trust and adoption, and formal model checking provides a rigorous method for verifying network behavior.

title: 基于本体论的动态知识图谱推理
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to knowledge reasoning utilizing a dynamic knowledge graph (DKG) grounded in an ontology. The core claim is that leveraging the semantic relationships within an ontology and the evolutionary mechanisms of a DKG can significantly enhance the flexibility and accuracy of inference capabilities. The proposed system employs a rule engine based on the ontology to drive dynamic reasoning and a suite of graph algorithms operating on the DKG to facilitate knowledge discovery. This integration offers a more intelligent method for both knowledge inference and knowledge management compared to traditional approaches. The system is designed to adapt to evolving knowledge landscapes, addressing limitations of static knowledge graphs. This paper details the architecture, algorithms, and key components, outlining a framework for building and operating such a system. The presented methodology provides a foundation for developing robust and adaptable knowledge reasoning systems, particularly in domains characterized by rapid change and complex relationships. ---
